title: Generic-fibre-trivial lines in a flat integral-fibre Noetherian family
statement: Let $f:Y\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume that $Y$ and $T$ are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and that $T$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and normal, meaning that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Assume that $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], that every residue-field fibre $Y_t=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is integral and nonempty [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-fibre-product], and that $f$ is either quasi-compact (the inverse image of each affine open is quasi-compact) or locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $T$, with residue field $K=\mathcal O_{T,\eta}$, and write $Y_\eta=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}K$. For an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $M$ [def-sc-invertible-module], assume that its tensor pullback to $Y_\eta$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{Y_\eta}$. Then there exist an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module $N$ and an isomorphism $f^*N\cong M$, where all pullbacks are tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, entire statement (hypotheses (1)--(5) and conclusion).

proof.text: First $Y$ is integral. Here are the affine details of Tag 0BCM. For a nonempty affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ mapping into an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset T$, $R$ is a domain and $B$ is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. By [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], $B\to B_K$ is injective: a fraction $b/1$ is zero only if some nonzero $r\in R$ kills $b$. Also $B_K\ne0$, since otherwise some nonzero $r$ kills $1_B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}B_K$ is the nonempty open $W_\eta$ in the integral fibre $Y_\eta$, so $B_K$ and hence $B$ are domains. Such $W$ form a basis; thus $Y$ is reduced and every nonempty open meets $Y_\eta$. Any two nonempty opens meet there since $Y_\eta$ is irreducible. Hence $Y$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, and is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. This is the elementary localization argument, not an assumption of geometric integrality.

source.place: Tag 0BCM, lemma-flat-over-integral-integral-fibre, applied in the opening paragraph of Tag 0BD7; affine localization and irreducibility details written out.

proof.text: Choose a generating section $s_\eta$ of $M|_{Y_\eta}$. Write $k(Y)$ for the function field of the integral scheme $Y$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], rings on nonempty affine opens embed in $k(Y)$. Localizing an affine ring $B$ over $R$ at $R\setminus\{0\}$ does not change its fraction field: every fraction in either ring is a fraction in $\operatorname{Frac}B$, and conversely $b/c$ is still a fraction of elements of $B_K$. Thus $Y$ and $Y_\eta$ have the same generic function field. The generic value of $s_\eta$ defines a nonzero rational section $s$ of $M$, meaning a nonzero vector in its one-dimensional generic fibre. In any local frame $v$ of $M$, write $s=qv$, $q\in k(Y)^\times$. Equality of these rational expressions detects equality of regular sections by the injectivity just cited. All base scalars in $K$ act through the injective maps of these function fields.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof, local-ring factorization and fibre-overlap argument; final globalization with the omitted gluing details supplied.

proof.text: Fix $x\in Y$, put $t=f(x)$, $A=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y,x}$, and choose a frame $v$ near $x$. The rings are Noetherian domains, and $A$ is normal. Noetherianity of these localizations follows by localizing finite generators of the contraction of any ideal. By [def-weil-flat-morphism] the stalk map $A\to B$ is flat and local, and by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] it is faithfully flat and surjective on spectra. For a prime of $A$ corresponding to a generalization $t'$ of $t$, its fibre is the localization of an affine open of $Y_{t'}$ at the functions inverted in passing to $B$. Indeed the affine fibre formula of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the fraction map $(b/a)\otimes c\mapsto(b\otimes c)/(a\otimes1)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] identify its ring with that localization. It is a domain since $Y_{t'}$ is integral, and is nonzero by surjectivity on spectra. The frame $v$ pulls back to a frame on $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and its generic fibre. The coefficient $q$ of $s$ in this frame is a unit of $B_K$: the given $s_\eta$ and its inverse in this frame restrict to that affine generic fibre. Apply [lem-sfb-local-generic-unit-factorization] to get $q=h_xu_x$, with $h_x\in K^\times$, $u_x\in B^\times$. Set $g_x=h_x^{-1}$. Then $f^*g_x\,s=u_xv$ is a regular generator near $x$, since the unit germ and its inverse have regular representatives on a neighbourhood.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof, local-ring factorization and fibre-overlap argument; final globalization with the omitted gluing details supplied.

proof.text: For any fixed $g\in K^\times$, let $W(g)$ be the locus where the rational section $f^*g\,s$ is a regular generator of $M$. This locus is open: in a local frame its coefficient must be a unit, and a unit germ together with its inverse spreads to a neighbourhood. It is saturated for $f$. To see this, suppose $x\in W(g)$ lies over $t$, and let $x'\in Y_t$. Step 3 supplies $g'\in K^\times$ and a neighbourhood $W'\ni x'$ on which $f^*g'\,s$ generates. The two nonempty opens $W(g)\cap Y_t$ and $W'\cap Y_t$ intersect since $Y_t$ is integral; take a point $z$ in their intersection. At $z$, their ratio $f^*(g/g')$ is a regular unit. The final clause of [lem-sfb-local-generic-unit-factorization], applied to $\mathcal O_{T,t}\to\mathcal O_{Y,z}$ with the hypotheses verified in step 3, gives $g/g'\in\mathcal O_{T,t}^{\times}$. Its pullback is a unit at $x'$, so $f^*g\,s$ generates at $x'$. Thus $W(g)=f^{-1}(V(g))$ for the subset $V(g)=f(W(g))$ of $T$. Here the topology of the scheme fibre agrees with the subspace fibre by [def-pc-scheme-fibre].

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof, local-ring factorization and fibre-overlap argument; final globalization with the omitted gluing details supplied.

proof.text: The map $f$ is surjective since all its fibres are nonempty. If $f$ is quasi-compact, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-qc-surjective-quotient-map] applied to $W(g)=f^{-1}(V(g))$ says that $V(g)$ is open. If $f$ is locally of finite type, choose Noetherian affine opens on $T$ and affine finite-type presentations on their inverse images. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], these algebra presentations are finite presentations, so $f$ is locally of finite presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], $f$ is open; hence again $V(g)=f(W(g))$ is open. For each $t$, choose $x$ above it and $g=g_x$ from step 3. Then $t\in V(g)$ and $f^*g\,s$ generates on all of $f^{-1}V(g)$. Choose one such pair $(V_i,g_i)$ for each $t$; the $V_i$ cover $T$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof, local-ring factorization and fibre-overlap argument; final globalization with the omitted gluing details supplied.

proof.text: On $V_i\cap V_j$, the rational function $a_{ij}=g_i/g_j$ is a regular unit. At any $t$ in the overlap, choose $x$ above $t$. Both $f^*g_i\,s$ and $f^*g_j\,s$ generate at $x$, so the unit-reflection clause of [lem-sfb-local-generic-unit-factorization] gives $a_{ij}\in\mathcal O_{T,t}^{\times}$. A rational function and its inverse which belong to a stalk have regular representatives near that point; the representatives agree on overlaps because their values in $K$ agree, by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. They therefore give a regular unit on the entire overlap. The identities $a_{ii}=1$ and $a_{ij}a_{jk}=a_{ik}$ hold as rational functions and hence as regular functions. Construct $N$ by gluing frames $n_i$ with $n_i=a_{ij}n_j$. Explicitly $N(V)$ consists of families $b_i\in\mathcal O_T(V\cap V_i)$ satisfying $b_j=b_i a_{ij}$ on overlaps, with componentwise restriction and module operations. The sheaf axiom follows componentwise from that of $\mathcal O_T$. On $V_i$ a family is determined by $b_i$ and the displayed cocycle determines all other components, so $N|_{V_i}\cong\mathcal O_{V_i}$. Thus $N$ is an invertible module in the sense of [def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof, local-ring factorization and fibre-overlap argument; final globalization with the omitted gluing details supplied.

proof.text: On $f^{-1}V_i$ define $f^*N\to M$ by sending the pulled-back frame $n_i$ to $f^*g_i\,s$. This is a module isomorphism because the latter is a regular generator. On overlaps, $n_i=a_{ij}n_j$ pulls back to the identical relation $f^*g_i\,s=f^*(a_{ij})f^*g_j\,s$; the tensor-pullback definition [def-pc-module-pullback] sends a scalar to its image under $f^\sharp$. Hence the maps and their inverses agree on overlaps and glue, by the sheaf axiom, to $f^*N\cong M$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NR-3e70bfa73 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. It has 7 steps, no new nodes and no re-split note; the item was statement-only on the base. I compared it against Stacks divisors.tex Tag 0BD7 (l.6968-7103) and Tag 0BCM (l.1735). Hypotheses (1)-(5) and the conclusion f*N≅M match the source exactly; nothing is weakened. Step 1: Y is integral by the explicit 0BCM argument (B is flat, so torsion-free, so B⊂B_K = the ring of W_η; Y is irreducible because every nonempty open meets the irreducible Y_η). Step 2: the rational section from s_η, using O_{T,η}=K, so Frac B = Frac B_K. Step 3: I checked every hypothesis of the factorization node at O_{T,t}→O_{Y,x}: both are Noetherian domains, A is normal, the map is flat and local. Each fibre ring is a localization of the ring of an affine open of the integral Y_t', and it is nonzero because the map is surjective on spectra (00HR). The orientation g=h^{-1} is correct. Step 4: saturation through the point z, using the irreducible fibre and the unit-reflection clause at O_{T,t}→O_{Y,z}; this matches the source's x'' argument. Step 5: the qc branch uses the 02JY quotient-map leaf; the lft branch uses 00FP on Noetherian charts to get lfp, then flat lfp is open, so lfp is never assumed from lft alone. Steps 6-7 supply the gluing the source omits: a_ij is a regular unit by unit reflection plus injectivity into K, the cocycle and the frame relation b_j=b_i a_ij are consistent, and the pullback isomorphism glues. Every hypothesis is used. Small cases checked: a field base, the DVR base with A^1 and vertical twists, the identity morphism, and a generic fibre that is not geometrically integral. Duplicate search (rg -L for 0BD7 and generic-fibre line terms): the factorization node is the local input; vertical-cartier-descent, space-valuation-line-triviality and modification-line-section-comparison state different results. Route: every off-unit statement is a mathlib-status leaf and the factorization node is in the same unit, so tool_uses=[] is fine. The report sentence claiming tool_uses were declared is inaccurate but immaterial. Batch-5: lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain is a pure-algebra Mathlib leaf (flat ⇒ torsion-free) and is accepted. The factorization node's 91-node closure reaches only lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel and def-trf-affine-weil-divisor-class-group, which are normal-domain divisor algebra and no step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality; accepted. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem normal_noetherian_generic_line_pullback {Y T : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ T) [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [IsLocallyNoetherian T] [IsIntegral T] (hnormal : ∀ t : T, IsDomain (T.presheaf.stalk t) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (T.presheaf.stalk t)) [Flat f] (hfibres : ∀ t : T, IsIntegral (pullback f (T.fromSpecResidueField t))) (hfinite : QuasiCompact f ∨ LocallyOfFiniteType f) (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] (hgeneric : Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f (T.fromSpecResidueField (genericPoint T)))).obj M ≅ SheafOfModules.unit (pullback f (T.fromSpecResidueField (genericPoint T))).ringCatSheaf)) : ∃ N : T.Modules, N.IsInvertible ∧ Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f).obj N ≅ M)
